symbols.name: currency
symbols.description: Explicit printed invoice currency. Leave absent when not printed; never infer it from a reference amount.

symbols.name: issuer_nif
symbols.description: NIF/CIF of the issuing supplier. Never the customer's (A58231074, Banco Miralmar).

symbols.name: issuer_name
symbols.description: Name of the issuer as printed. Trace only; no rule decides with it.

symbols.name: iban
symbols.description: Payment IBAN printed on the invoice.

symbols.name: date
symbols.description: Issue date as YYYY-MM-DD with the printed numbers, uncorrected: 31/02/2026 -> "2026-02-31". Accepts DD/MM/YYYY and '6 de abril de 2026'. Never None because the date is impossible.

symbols.name: total
symbols.description: Printed total (TOTAL, IMPORTE TOTAL, TOTAL A PAGAR, Total factura). Not Subtotal nor 'Suma y sigue'.

symbols.name: free_text
symbols.description: Text that is not a header, a line item or totals (notes, notices, terms). Always stored. No rule reads it: it only feeds the embedded-instructions warning in the trace.

rules.summary: Invoice has all the required fields
rules.text: The symbols `issuer_nif`, `iban`, `purchase_order`, `date`, `base`, `vat_rate`, `vat_amount` and `total` are all other than `None`. Reason: list of the missing ones.
There is at least one row in `suppliers` whose normalised `nif` equals the normalised `issuer_nif`.

rules.summary: Bank account matches the registered supplier
rules.text: If there are rows in `suppliers` with that `nif`, and all of them have the same `id` and normalised `iban`, then that `iban` equals the normalised `iban` of the invoice, or differs from it in more than 4 characters. If there are no rows, it does not fire (R02). If the rows disagree with each other, it does not fire (R04). A difference of at most 4 characters is a misreading rather than another account: R17 escalates it.

rules.summary: Supplier is registered more than once with different details
rules.text: There are two or more rows in `suppliers` with the same normalised `nif` as `issuer_nif` and a different `id` or a different normalised `iban` (identical repeated rows do NOT count).
There is a row in `orders` whose `purchase_order` equals the `purchase_order` of the invoice.

rules.summary: Purchase order belongs to this supplier
rules.text: With the `orders` row of that `purchase_order`: if `orders.nif` is not empty, it equals `issuer_nif`; if it is empty, `orders.supplier_id` equals the `id` of the `suppliers` row with `nif = issuer_nif` (if that row does not exist, it does not fire).

rules.summary: Invoice total matches the purchase order
rules.text: With the `orders` row of that `purchase_order`: `total` matches `orders.total_amount` (±0.01). The **total** of the invoice is compared, not the base. Skip this comparison when an explicit currency other than EUR is printed: a foreign total is converted only by R18, and a difference measured in another currency never refuses a payment.

`vat_amount` matches (±0.01) `round(base * vat_rate / 100, 2)`, using the printed `vat_rate`. Only on an invoice in EUR or with no printed currency: on a foreign invoice the same arithmetic is R18's, which escalates instead of refusing.

rules.summary: VAT rate is not the standard 21%

rules.text: `total` matches (±0.01) `base + vat_amount`, using the printed values. The text of the invoice does not change the calculation.

rules.summary: Invoice date is a real date
rules.text: `date` is a real calendar date (valid `YYYY-MM-DD`: month 1-12 and a day that exists in that month and year).

rules.summary: Invoice is dated after the cut-off date
rules.text: If `date` is valid: `date` is later than `parameters.cut_off_date`.

rules.summary: Purchase order is in the ERP
rules.text: There is a row in `erp` whose `purchase_order` equals `purchase_order`. Only evaluated if R05 does not fire.

rules.summary: ERP record matches the purchase order
rules.text: For every `erp` row of that `purchase_order`, compared with its `orders` row: `erp.amount` matches `orders.total_amount` (±0.01) **and** `erp.supplier_id` equals `orders.supplier_id` **and**, if both `nif` are not empty, they are equal. Reason: fields that differ.

rules.summary: Invoice is already paid in the ERP
rules.text: Any matching `erp` row has a nonempty status other than `PENDIENTE`. A later pending row must never hide a paid entry; row order cannot change the result.

rules.summary: Another invoice uses the same purchase order
rules.text: There is at least one instance in `others` with the same normalised `purchase_order`. Each instance in `others` is identified by its `_instance` key (its file name). Reason: the `_instance` values with that purchase order.

rules.summary: Bank account looks like a misread of the registered one
rules.text: The normalised `iban` of the invoice differs from the one account the master approves for that `nif` in at least 1 and at most 4 characters. Reason: both accounts and how many characters apart they are.

rules.summary: Foreign currency that cannot be compared with confidence
rules.text: An invoice with an explicitly printed currency other than EUR goes to a person when any of these holds: the printed code is not a three-letter currency code; there is no row in `rates` for that currency whose `as_of`..`valid_until` covers `date` (the rate in force on the invoice's own date, never the nearest one, and never a clock: `rates` may hold several rows for one currency with non-overlapping windows, since a rate change is a new row and a row is never edited); converting `total` with that row's `eur_per_unit` differs from `orders.total_amount` of its `purchase_order` by more than `max(0.01, converted * tolerance_pct / 100)`, which with the published `tolerance_pct` of 0 is the norm's own cent: each rate reproduces its order exactly, and a currency that ever needs a wider band gets it by a new row, not by new code; or `vat_amount` does not match (±0.01) `round(base * vat_rate / 100, 2)`. It does NOT fire when the invoice is already refusable on its own data, so that a refusal is not turned into a review: `total` does not match `base + vat_amount` (±0.01), or its `iban` differs in more than 4 characters from the single account the master approves for its `nif`. Money is only compared inside one currency, and no exchange rate is ever inferred from an order or an ERP amount. Missing printed currency keeps the existing v3 treatment. Reason: the currency and every finding.
